title: RISC-V Instruction Set Extensions for Multi-Precision Integer Arithmetic: A Case Study on Post-Quantum Key Exchange Using CSIDH-512
problem: Multi-precision integer (MPI) arithmetic is a performance bottleneck in public-key cryptosystems including post-quantum schemes. The paper compares full-radix and reduced-radix MPI representations to identify efficient implementations for 64-bit RISC-V modular arithmetic operations.
motivation: Optimizing multi-precision arithmetic through hardware instruction extensions can significantly accelerate post-quantum cryptographic operations on RISC-V processors.
method: Multi-precision integer arithmetic—calculations with numbers too large to fit in a single 64-bit register—is slow because processors lack specialized instructions for it. The paper tests two ways of representing these large numbers (full-radix and reduced-radix) on 64-bit RISC-V to identify which is faster, then designs custom processor instructions that directly execute the specific arithmetic operations (multiplication and modular reduction) used in CSIDH-512 cryptography. These custom instructions are built into a Rocket processor core and tested to measure performance gains.
key_novelty: The core idea is adding processor instructions optimized for the multi-precision arithmetic that post-quantum cryptography requires.
contributions: Comparative analysis of full-radix and reduced-radix MPI representations for RISC-V
Design of custom instruction set extensions for multi-precision modular arithmetic
1.71x speedup on CSIDH-512 class group action implementation
Hardware-software co-design evaluation with 10% area overhead
limitations: Generalization to other post-quantum schemes and comparison with alternative acceleration approaches are not discussed.
primary_theme: ISE design for post-quantum cryptographic acceleration
